narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Night Harbour"**

Svall looks like a harbour at night. The sea is a calm, dark blue-slate. The chrome around it is sand and cream. The robots on their cards carry the color, so status is the loudest thing on screen and reads at a glance: working, blocked or done, from across the room. Everything else stays quiet.

The app is a tool people keep open all day. It is dense but calm: small type on a fixed scale, cream hairlines, glass over the map, solid surfaces for dialogs. Controls are warm and tactile: a sand primary button, cream fills that light under the pointer, a chip pressed in sand, buttons that give a little when pressed.

All values come from `apps/desktop/web/src/tokens.css`. All repeated controls are one primitive each, mostly in `base.css`. The phone app and svall.dev load the same tokens.
keyCharacteristics: One blue-slate family for every surface, one cream family for every ink, sand for what is active or primary.
Status colors belong to robots; they stay apart under color blindness, and beyond the sidebar's dots each comes with its word.
The map is scenery: textured, quiet, no loud rings on its pills.
Every text and icon is checked against the ground it is drawn on.

rules.name: The Accent Rule
rules.body: Sand means focus, active, current or primary, and the text cursor. Blue means a selected item, a drop target, a link or selected text. Never swap them, and never use either as decoration.

rules.name: The Robots Carry the Color Rule
rules.body: Working, blocked, done, idle, moving and unknown use the same token in the app, the phone, the board card, the map card and the site. Where a status shows as color alone (the sidebar's dots), any two stay apart under protanopia and deuteranopia (ΔE2000 of 10 or more); everywhere else it also carries its word or a shape. Chrome uses a status color only for the same meaning, such as the coral count of robots that need you.

rules.name: The Contrast Floor Rule
rules.body: Text and icons hold 4.5:1 against the ground they are drawn on, including hover and selected fills and glass over the map. Large text, and non-text UI (field borders, focus rings, status dots, selected rings, a glyph beside its own label) hold 3:1. ink-3 is the dimmest ink for text. Disabled controls, at `--disabled` (.45), are exempt.

rules.name: The One Source Rule
rules.body: Colors live only in `tokens.css`. Stylesheets and scripts use `var(--…)` or a `color-mix()` of tokens; `test/tokens.test.ts` fails on a raw hex or `rgb()` anywhere else (the robot body colors in `portraits.ts` mirror their drawings and are the exception). The site's page tokens are mixed from the app's.

rules.name: The Rung Rule
rules.body: No font size, weight or tracking outside its token rung.

rules.name: The Calm Map Rule
rules.body: On the map a selected pill (an island's label, the resources pill) brightens its border to line-strong and its glass to glass-hi; it never wears a blue ring. The board card keeps its blue selection ring.

dos: Do build new UI from the primitives above (`.ib`, `.seg`, `.dtab`, `.pill`, `.btn.sm`, `.list-row`, `.menu-item`, `.menu`, `.count`, `.banner`, `.dialog`, `.popover`, `.panel`, `.width-grip`, `.sec-grip`) and icons from `icons.tsx`.
Do write CSS in the house style: one rule per line, `prop: value;` with a space after the colon, wrapped by hand when long, token values only.
Do add a token only when a value repeats or two places must match.
Do measure contrast where the color is drawn, on the real ground, in hover and selected states too.
Do give a status its word or shape wherever it is more than a dot.
Do comment only what the code cannot say, in a line or two.
donts: Don't put a raw color in a stylesheet or script, or a raw spacing, radius, type size, duration or easing in a stylesheet.
Don't use blue for focus or sand for selection.
Don't put a blue ring on a map pill.
Don't use a text glyph as an icon, or centre an icon with padding or line height.
Don't write a one-off button, chip, row or menu when a primitive fits.
Don't set text dimmer than ink-3.
